support_files.docstring: Run core/focused checks, an explicit tier, or unfiltered --full acceptance.
Share immutable code objects while retaining real source/binding admission.

Functional units with independently owned scenario fixtures.

Scenario assertions still run as subtests, without creating nested unittest
runs or reporting old method executions as new discovered tests. Mutable
windows, directories, tensors and cleanup stacks remain scenario-local.

Cap the memory one test may commit, so a runaway test fails on its own.

Each test may commit ``budget`` bytes beyond what its process held when the
test started. Going over makes the allocation fail (``MemoryError`` from NumPy
or Python, an allocation error from Torch) inside that test, which then reports
the traceback, instead of the process taking the machine's memory.

Windows only: a job object caps the process's committed private memory, and
the cap is moved at the start of every test. Windows charges CUDA allocations
to that commit as well, so the budget covers GPU and host memory together.
Elsewhere nothing is enforced and ``install`` says so.

Observe selected Python boundaries without profiling unrelated calculations.

The callbacks retain the existing ``(frame, event, arg)`` convention. Python
3.12's local monitoring events leave the actual functions, aliases and code
identities intact, unlike wrapping the functions with mocks.
Isolated full-suite workers with exhaustive assignment and fail-closed results.
Explicit review declarations for synthetic complete-outline test fixtures.

Explicit test selections; full discovery is always the union, unfiltered.

CPU/Qt is an allowlist, not an inference from skip decorators. CUDA contains
every remaining ID, so new tests cannot disappear from full CI. Core
intentionally overlaps the two exhaustive partition groups.
Internal isolated unittest worker; the full controller owns its manifest.
